For context, `AppPreview.tsx`, `AppNavCanvas.tsx`, `preview-registry.ts` and `i18n.ts` were read at the head and at the base through `contents/…?ref=`, and the spec's `resolveI18nLabel` source (`packages/spec/src/ui/i18n-label-resolver.ts`) was read for its miss semantics. Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

Diff: `AppPreview.tsx` (+17/−9), new pin `AppPreview.labelMaps-11100.test.tsx` (7 tests), one changeset. Public surface: `AppPreview`'s props are unchanged (`MetadataPreviewProps`), `normalizeNav` and `I18nText` stay module-private, no new export, no new dependency (`resolveI18nLabel` was already imported from `@objectstack/spec/ui` for `readAreas`). Right: nothing public moves.

1. **App label (site 1).** Base `:239` `(draft as any).label ?? appName`, rendered at `:304` as `{String(label)}`. Head `:247` `resolveI18nLabel(draft.label as I18nText, locale) ?? appName`, rendered at `:312` as `{label}`. The `String()` call is gone; the read follows the typed-draft pattern `readAreas` already uses in this file (`draft` is typed as a record of unknown values in `MetadataPreviewProps`, so no new any-cast). A map resolves in the designer locale; `appName` fires only when the resolver answers `undefined` (label absent, or a map with no string entry). A plain string, `''` included, comes back unchanged, so the control holds. Right.

2. **Nav-item label (site 2).** Base `:137` `typeof it.label === 'string' ? it.label.trim() : ''`. Head `:143` `(resolveI18nLabel(it.label, locale) ?? '').trim()`. `locale` is threaded as a required positional `string | undefined` (the spec's own rule for this resolver, and the shape `readAreas` takes), passed into the recursion at `:162`, and added to the `useMemo` deps at `:268` so a locale switch re-resolves the nav. Under `en-US` the map `{en, zh-CN}` resolves through the resolver's base-language limb to `Accounts`; under `zh-CN` through the exact limb to `客户`. Right.

3. **Group label (site 3).** Same path: a group's map label resolves, and `label || unnamed` at `:163` now fires only on an empty resolved text. Right.

4. **Keep/drop rule.** Base dropped an entry on `!label && !it.children`, before the target was even read. Head reads `navTarget(it, kind)` first and drops only on `!label && !it.children && !target` (`:144–145`). Judged against the triage ("a nav item is kept whenever it has a target; its label only decides the text, never whether the item exists"): an entry with a target is now unconditionally kept, whatever its label. Entries with a label or with children were never dropped before and are not now; only the entry with nothing to show (no label, no children, no target) is dropped, as before. Right.
   The behaviour change the dev names, an entry that names a record but carries no label used to vanish and now reads `(unnamed)`, IS the triage's rule rather than a departure from it: "kept whenever it has a target" is stated with no condition on the label, and "`(unnamed)` stays only for a label that is truly absent" names the text such an entry gets. The two rulings compose to exactly this outcome, and the changeset tells the author. Right.

5. **A map resolving to nothing.** `resolveI18nLabel({}, locale)` walks all six limbs, finds no string entry and answers `undefined` (never `''`, never a stringified object); the head folds that to `''`, so the row reads `(unnamed)` and keeps its target. Pinned by the `deals` case. Right: that is "truly absent" as far as the designer can show anything, and no `[object Object]` path remains, since neither site calls `String()` on a label and the resolver refuses a non-map object rather than stringifying it.

6. **The pins.** Seven cases: map app / nav-item / group labels under `en-US` and `zh-CN` (resolved text present, the item keeps its `account` target, the group keeps its child, the landing line reads the resolved label, neither locale's `(unnamed)` string appears, no `[object Object]` in the body); plain strings as the control; an app with no label falls to its name; `(unnamed)` for a truly absent label and for an empty map under both locales, with `lead` and `deal` kept and the empty `ghost` entry dropped; and the app label in design mode. The `navRow` helper reads the row through the label span's `parentElement`, which is the `NavRow` div carrying the kind and target spans (`:415–425`), so the target assertions address the right element. The pin file follows the directory's `Name.topic-NNNN.test.tsx` convention and imports `../i18n` the way `AppPreview.areas-11027.test.tsx` does. Right; the pins are the card's pins line.

Nothing else in the diff. No accept-set moves on the spec side: the preview now honours what `I18nLabelSchema` already accepted.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/11100-app-preview-label-maps.md`: `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`. Right: a rendering fix to the Studio preview with no prop, type, export or schema change; the one visible behaviour change (a targeted, label-less entry shown as `(unnamed)` instead of hidden) is a fix in the direction the card ruled, and the changeset text states it. The changeset prose matches the code (kept when it names a record or holds children; `(unnamed)` for an absent or unresolvable label; the app name when no label is authored). ### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (three), open_questions (none), one out-of-scope finding.

a. **PR assignee write refused.** `label-write --assign os-support-ai` was denied by the dev's own permission layer before any request left; PR #11127 has no assignee (read: empty `assignees`), and its labels are the path labeler's `tests` and `package: app-shell` only. Observation only, as the brief frames it: the card is assigned to `os-support-ai`; the seat sets the PR assignee. Not a contract breach.

b. **Attribution trailer.** The two commits (`2f2a7933d`, `cbe37f8b2`) carry `Claude-Session:` and a model-free `Co-authored-by: Claude` pair; no model identifier appears in any commit, the PR title or body, the changeset or the report. Conforms to the repo rule. Answered.

c. **Base moved.** The order measured `cff8641e2`; the PR's base is `76e9df06c`. `compare/cff8641e2...76e9df06c` is one commit (#11121, objectui#11082) touching 7 files, none under `metadata-admin/previews/`; the three sites read at `76e9df06c` are the card's, line for line (`:137`, `:157`, `:304`). `main` is still `76e9df06c` at review time. Answered; no rebase owed.

d. **Out-of-scope finding: `AppNavCanvas.tsx` `navLabel` in design mode.** Confirmed by reading at the head: `navLabel` (`:164–169`) tests `typeof l === 'string' && l.trim()` and otherwise returns the positional `Item N`; `RawNav.label` is typed `string` only (`:50`). So a map-labelled nav item in design mode (editing) shows `Item 1` in the canvas row while the header's landing line (this PR) shows the resolved text; the dev's probe reads right. Same family as this card: the spec's `AppSchema.navigation[].label` (`I18nLabel`) read through a string test, exactly site 2's defect, in the design-mode renderer of the same nav. Pre-existing: the file is byte-identical at base and head, last touched 2026-08-20 (#5383), and untouched by this PR. Not widened here, rightly: the card names three sites in `AppPreview.tsx`, the dispatch surface was that file alone, and the canvas is an inline-rename editor whose write path (`renameItem` writes a plain string over `label`, `:263–264`; the dev's read-only inference, not measured) needs its own ruling before a fix. Escalated to the seat: file a sibling card for `AppNavCanvas.navLabel` (dedupe words: `AppNavCanvas`, `navLabel`, `Item 1`) and rule the rename-over-map write path there; objectui#10862 is queued on this file family and is the natural serial neighbour. This PR's design-mode pin covers the header only, as it should.
